topics.title: About you
topics.purpose: This screen collects the few details that decide your budget and what you'll pay for services.
steps: Enter your suburb and postcode.
Choose your level from your My Aged Care approval letter.
Choose your pension status from your DVA or Services Australia letter.
If you're a part pensioner, enter the two rates from your contribution letter, or use a range until it arrives.
Say whether you hold a DVA card.
Save your details.
topics.outcome: Your contribution rates and budget appear in the summary, and the other screens can work out costs.

faqs.q: Why do you need my postcode?
faqs.a: To match providers that service your area. Nothing else.

faqs.q: I don't have my contribution letter yet.
faqs.a: Leave the rates blank. The app shows costs as a range from the lowest to highest rate for your pension status until you enter them.

faqs.q: Who can see these details?
faqs.a: Only the family members your administrator has given access to this assessment.

troubleshooting.fix: Look for the messages under the fields marked in red.

topics.title: Your budget and the rules
topics.purpose: This screen shows your budget, how much is left for services, what you pay, and the rules behind those numbers.
steps: Check the money for your services each quarter.
Look at what you'd pay for each kind of service.
Read the rules that changed recently.
topics.outcome: You know how much you have to spend on services and roughly what you'll pay yourself.

faqs.q: Why is 10% taken off?
faqs.a: Your provider keeps 10% of each quarterly budget for care management: organising and reviewing your care.

faqs.q: What happens if I don't spend it all?
faqs.a: Up to $1,000 or 10% of your quarterly budget (whichever is more) carries into the next quarter.

troubleshooting.fix: Choose your level on the About you screen.

topics.title: What I'm looking for in a provider
topics.purpose: Your answers describe what you want from a provider. They decide which interview questions you need, feed the summary Claude can draft, and go in the dossier you give providers.
steps: Open each group and choose the answers that fit. Some questions let you choose several.
Add more detail in your own words under any question.
When you've answered what you can, ask Claude to draft a summary of what you're looking for, then check and edit it.
Mark a question "Not relevant to me" to drop the interview questions it covers.
topics.outcome: Your interview pack contains only the questions that matter to you, plus every must-ask question.

faqs.q: Do I have to answer them all?
faqs.a: No. Unanswered questions keep their interview questions in, just in case.

faqs.q: What does Not relevant to me do?
faqs.a: It drops the interview sections that question covers, but only when every question covering that section is not relevant. Must-ask questions always stay.

faqs.q: Is the summary sent anywhere?
faqs.a: Drafting it sends your answers, care plan and the details in About you to Anthropic's Claude to write the summary. Nothing goes to a provider unless you print a dossier and give it to them.

topics.title: Compare the cost of your care plan
topics.purpose: This screen works out what your weekly care plan would cost each quarter at each provider, and what you'd pay yourself.
steps: Check the care plan: services and hours each week.
Look at the chart to see which providers fit your services budget.
Check what you'd pay at each provider.
Compare each provider's prices with the guide price.
topics.outcome: You know which providers are cheapest for your plan and whether any fit your budget.

faqs.q: Why 13 weeks?
faqs.a: A quarter is 13 weeks. Budgets are set per quarter, so costs are too.

faqs.q: What does filled from benchmark mean?
faqs.a: The provider hasn't published a price for that service, so the guide price is used instead. Ask them at interview.

faqs.q: Why is what I pay a range?
faqs.a: Until your exact contribution rates are entered, the app shows the lowest and highest you could pay.

troubleshooting.cause: The plan needs more hours than your budget pays for
troubleshooting.fix: Reduce hours, ask DVA about services it could fund, or check any carried-over funds.

troubleshooting.symptom: A provider isn't in the chart
troubleshooting.cause: They haven't published prices for the services in your plan
troubleshooting.fix: Ask them to cost your plan (interview question G7).

topics.title: Providers near you
topics.purpose: Look up providers that service your area, check their prices and keep notes.
steps: Search or filter the list.
Open a provider to see their prices, flags and notes.
Add the ones worth a look to your list.
topics.outcome: A first list of providers worth a closer look.

faqs.q: Where do the prices come from?
faqs.a: Each provider's published price list, linked as the source. Check the date: prices older than 60 days may have changed.

faqs.q: A price is wrong.
faqs.a: Open the provider and choose Edit details and prices. Everyone in the family sees the change.

troubleshooting.cause: They weren't in the starting data
troubleshooting.fix: Add them with Add provider, or import a spreadsheet.

topics.title: Choose who to meet
topics.purpose: Narrow down from all providers to the few you'll interview, in three steps.
steps: Initial scan: keep anyone worth a second look.
Refinement: compare costs and flags, and aim for 3 to 5.
Providers to interview: put them in order and note why, and what to watch for.
topics.outcome: A short, ordered list of providers to interview, with your reasons.

faqs.q: Can I change my mind?
faqs.a: Yes. Move providers back a step, or drop them and use Undo.

faqs.q: How many should I interview?
faqs.a: At least two, so you can compare. Three is common.

topics.title: Your interview questions
topics.purpose: Your questions for each provider, ready to use during interviews or to print.
steps: Choose the provider you're interviewing.
Ask each question and write down the answer.
Mark whether it was answered well and whether you got it in writing.
Print the pack if you prefer paper.
topics.outcome: Each provider's answers recorded in one place, ready for scoring.

faqs.q: What if a provider won't answer a must-ask question?
faqs.a: Write that down. The scoring screen flags any provider that leaves a must-ask question without a written answer.

troubleshooting.cause: No one is on the interview list yet
troubleshooting.fix: Move providers to Providers to interview.

topics.title: Record an interview
topics.purpose: Record or note an interview, then turn it into notes you can check and keep.
steps: Confirm everyone agrees to the recording.
Record, or type notes instead.
Check and correct the transcript.
Draft notes, check them, and save the ones you want.
topics.outcome: Checked notes saved against the provider.

faqs.q: Where is the recording kept?
faqs.a: Only on the device that made it. The transcript and notes are shared with your family.

faqs.q: Who drafts the notes?
faqs.a: Claude, an AI model, from the transcript only. Check them before saving.

troubleshooting.fix: Allow microphone access in the browser's site settings, or type notes instead.

topics.title: Score and decide
topics.purpose: Score each provider you met and see how they compare.
steps: Score each provider from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent) on each criterion.
Change what counts most if you need to.
Check the ranking and any disqualify warnings.
Write down your decision and make the summary.
topics.outcome: A ranked list and a written decision you can share with family.

faqs.q: Does the top score decide for me?
faqs.a: No. It's a guide. The decision is yours.

faqs.q: What does Disqualify? mean?
faqs.a: The provider left a must-ask question without a satisfactory written answer.

glossary.plain: The Australian Government program that pays for care at home for older people. It replaced Home Care Packages on 1 November 2025.

The level of support you were approved for, from 1 to 8, shown on your My Aged Care approval letter. Higher levels come with a bigger budget. People who moved over from a Home Care Package keep their package level instead.
The amount the government sets aside for your care each three months (a quarter). Budgets are indexed each 1 July.
Your provider keeps 10% of each quarterly budget to organise your care: planning, check-ins and coordination. The rest is money for your services.
glossary.example: Of a $10,808 quarterly budget, $1,081 goes to care management and $9,727 is left for services.

glossary.plain: The share of each service's price you pay yourself. It depends on the type of service and your pension status. Clinical care is always free.

The three kinds of service. Clinical care (nursing, and personal care from 1 October 2026) costs you nothing. Independence services (like social support) and Everyday living services (like cleaning and gardening) have a contribution that depends on your pension.

How the government assessed your income and assets. Full pensioners pay the lowest contribution rates. Part pensioners pay a rate set in their letter. Self-funded retirees, and people who don't disclose their means, pay the highest rates.
If you were approved for a Home Care Package on or before 12 September 2024, you pay no more than you would have under the old rules: lower contribution rates and a lower lifetime cap.
Once your non-clinical contributions reach the cap, you stop paying them. The cap is $140,652.80 (or $88,934.57 under no-worse-off) as at 20 September 2026, and it is shared with residential care.
Money you don't spend in a quarter can carry into the next, up to $1,000 or 10% of your quarterly budget, whichever is more.
The price the Independent Health and Aged Care Pricing Authority advises for each service in 2026-27. It is advice, not a cap: providers set their own prices.
You get all your Support at Home services from one registered provider. That provider can subcontract some services to others.
A DVA program for Gold and some White Card holders: help with cleaning, garden, personal care and respite. Using it can save your Support at Home budget. DVA decides who is eligible.
DVA health cards. A Gold Card covers all health care needs; a White Card covers care for specific accepted conditions.
Assistive technology and home modifications: equipment like rails and ramps, and changes to your home. They have a separate budget and aren't costed in this app.
The date a provider's price list was collected. Providers must review prices at least every two months, so prices older than 60 days may be out of date.
A question every provider must answer in writing. If a provider won't, treat that as a warning sign.
Questions about your situation that decide which interview questions you need. In the program documents they're called bounding questions.
The average of the scores you gave a provider, with the criteria that matter most counted more. It helps rank providers; the decision is still yours.

fields.label: Suburb
fields.hint: Where you live, so we can match providers that service your area.

fields.label: Your level
fields.hint: The level on your My Aged Care approval letter, from 1 to 8. If you moved over from a Home Care Package, choose your package level under Transitioned Home Care Package.
fields.example_template: Level {classification} gives {quarterly} a quarter. After 10% care management, {for_services} is left for services.

fields.label: Your pension
fields.hint: As shown on your DVA or Services Australia income and assets letter.

fields.label: Your contribution rates
fields.hint: Part pensioners: the two percentages on your Support at Home contribution letter. DVA assesses DVA pensioners.

fields.label: Approved for a Home Care Package on or before 12 September 2024?
fields.hint: If yes, the no-worse-off principle gives lower rates and a lower lifetime cap.

fields.label: DVA card
fields.hint: The health card DVA issued, if any.

fields.label: Contributions paid so far
fields.hint: Non-clinical aged care contributions you've already paid, over your lifetime. Enter 0 if you're new to aged care.

fields.label: Hours a week
fields.hint: In quarter hours: 0.25 is 15 minutes, 0.5 is half an hour.
